data.gender_notes: Azmal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Azmal is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Aham' meaning 'I' and 'Zama' meaning 'Will'. It symbolizes the power of an individual's will, guided by the divine will of the universe. The name Azmal carries the meaning “God's Will” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Azmal usually hope their child will grow to embody god's will and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Azmal is a rare Hindu name with a rich cultural heritage. The name is not commonly used, making it unique and special for those that bear it. The fusion of 'Aham' and 'Zama' in Azmal represents the devotion and dedication of an individual towards their journey of self-realization and self-improvement. The name's cultural impact lies in its ability to inspire those who hear or come across it, reminding them of the power of will and self-determination.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of Azmal is rooted in the powerful combination of 'Aham' and 'Zama'. 'Aham' represents the individual self, while 'Zama' represents the divine will. This combination symbolizes the idea that an individual's will is guided and supported by the divine will of the universe. Azmal, therefore, serves as a reminder that one's actions and decisions are not made in isolation but in the context of the larger cosmic plan. This spiritual significance imbues the name with a deep sense of purpose and meaning, inspiring those who bear it to live virtuous and meaningful lives informed by a deep sense of spiritual awareness.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Azmal was the eldest son of the Rajput king Raja Jaswant Singh of Jodhpur, born in 1526. The name Azmal carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Azmal was also a famous Hindu military commander in the army of Raja Jai Singh II of Amer (Jaipur), during the late 17th and early 18th century.
